fit.gap_handling_summary: The outputs make good use of adjacent CI/CD, environment automation and observability experience while correctly identifying Terraform and certificate-management work as personal projects. They do not invent AWS, Terragrunt, mTLS, fleet integration or architecture leadership. However, the application leaves the largest readiness gaps largely implicit rather than briefly explaining the candidate's transition and the limits of the match to an independently operating contractor role.

issues: The professional experience and selected projects repeat the same environment automation, pipeline timings and runner-cost results.
The second page is only 22% filled, despite a dense first page.
The CI Pipeline Speed-up project heading is stranded at the bottom of page one, with all its bullets on page two.

The original 'Kubernetes (basic)' qualifier is omitted from the skills list. The accompanying shared-cluster and test-environment descriptions remain appropriately bounded, but retaining the qualifier would improve calibration.

reasons: The single-column PDF extracts in sensible order with intact words and standard headings.
The CV contains Terraform, Linux, TLS and observability evidence, with cert-manager providing a clear semantic match to certificate management.
AWS, Terragrunt and mTLS are absent, as are demonstrated production cloud architecture and technical-proposal leadership.
The headline and work history correctly retain the QA background, which is likely to rank below established cloud infrastructure contractors for this engagement.
Coverage counts obvious semantic matches such as cert-manager for certificate management and 'reliability' for reliable operation; it does not treat Java test automation as JVM backend experience.

issues: The second paragraph repeats ownership of infrastructure supporting three product teams without adding evidence.
The closing repeats the CI/CD, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability and TLS list already developed in the body.
It gives little explanation of readiness for independent architecture and production ownership, despite the role's senior scope.
The key gaps in major-cloud experience, Terragrunt and mTLS are left implicit. A short, candid transition statement would make the pitch more persuasive than another skills list.
Company specificity is accurate but limited mainly to engineering-led culture and end-to-end ownership.
strengths: Names Corvale Mobility and the exact Fleet Connectivity contractor role.
Uses supported, quantified delivery results rather than generic claims of DevOps expertise.
Clearly separates professional CI/CD and Kubernetes work from the personal homelab and Terraform projects.
Accurately states the candidate's intention to move into DevOps and platform engineering full time.
Uses the company's engineering-led approach and end-to-end ownership without inventing culture or benefits.

spacing_issues: CV page one is dense, while page two contains only the pipeline-project bullets, education and languages and is approximately 22% filled.
The CI Pipeline Speed-up heading is orphaned at the foot of page one; its first bullet appears on the next page.
Repeated employment/project content contributes to the inefficient page break and large unused area on page two.
issues: The 10-point CV body and closely packed bullets make the first page relatively demanding to skim, although all content remains legible.
The letter is cleanly set on one page with an 11-point body and comfortable margins.
The documents share a consistent serif style, but the CV needs rebalancing rather than further font reduction.

fluency_and_tone_issues: 'This work enabled QA and product teams to review features before merge while I owned the pipeline and environment automation supporting three product teams.' The final clause is repetitive and makes an otherwise clear achievement sentence cumbersome.

'how my experience in test infrastructure and hands-on experience in CI/CD, Kubernetes test environments, Terraform-based infrastructure, observability, and TLS certificate management could contribute' is a long, repetitive closing list.

parsed.summary: The application is factually disciplined and makes strong use of quantified CI/CD improvements, environment automation and monitoring work. It correctly labels the homelab and Terraform experience as personal rather than presenting them as production cloud employment. The real match remains limited for an independent architecture-heavy contractor role, particularly in AWS, Terragrunt, mTLS and technical leadership, and the letter does little to address that transition directly. The main presentation defect is the dense first CV page followed by a mostly empty second page, including a project heading separated from all its bullets.
